name: Poorcel face-pulling method

lead: The Poorcel face-pulling method is a homemade technique from looksmax.org. Users with limited budgets (the 'poorcel' label) describe improvised setups that put steady force on the teeth or jaw, with the stated aim of pulling the midface or jaw forward, widening the palate and correcting asymmetry.

The idea borrows from orthodontic facemask treatment, where a clinician uses a reverse-pull headgear to move the upper jaw forward in children. The home versions are forum inventions and no published study has tested them.

paras: Forum posts describe applying directional forces to the dental arch in the direction a person wants their palate to widen or grow, in some cases framed as imitating the jaw action of tearing raw meat. Details vary from post to post and are not given here.

Improvised force on teeth and jaws can move teeth, strain the joints or damage the bite. Orthodontic protraction headgear is prescribed and monitored by a clinician, and uses defined wear schedules under supervision.

angle.text: Users say steady pulling forces could move the palate or jaw in the direction of the pull, widening the jaw and projecting the face forward. This outcome has not been shown in published research.

lead: The Poorcel face-pulling method, also called the facepulling method, is a do-it-yourself technique shared on looksmax.org. 'Poorcel' in forum slang refers to a user who lacks the money for professional treatment, and the method is presented as a low-cost alternative. Its stated goals are to pull the face forward, widen the jaw and fix asymmetry by applying directional force to the dental arch [1].

The term 'face pulling' in the community draws on orthodontic maxillary protraction, where a reverse-pull facemask uses elastics attached to the teeth and a frame resting on the forehead and chin to push the upper jaw forward and down, to treat an underbite [2]. The forum methods are not orthodontic treatment, and no studies have tested them.

paras: Forum threads describe approaches that apply force to the dental arch to widen the palate, correct asymmetry or bring the whole jaw forward; one poster describes it as a final method alongside an earlier 'face pulling to bring the whole jaw forward' and compares it to the way predators tear raw meat [1]. Responses in threads vary from interest to scepticism.

In orthodontics, a reverse-pull facemask treats an upper jaw positioned too far back. It uses a metal bar in front of the face supported by pads on the forehead and chin, with elastics to the teeth that pull the jaw forward and down; wear time of 14 to 16 hours a day is described [2]. A clinician sets and monitors the treatment, usually in growing patients.

No studies found. Research on orthodontic facemask protraction in children exists, including a randomised trial reporting that early treatment reduced the need for orthognathic surgery, but it concerns supervised orthodontic devices rather than improvised methods [2].

lore.intro: The method is posted on looksmax.org as an inexpensive route to jaw and midface changes.

claims.claim: Directional force on the dental arch can widen the palate and fix asymmetry
